newsitem.title: MEXICO: DNA test confirms death of drug lord Amado Carrillo.
newsitem.headline: DNA test confirms death of drug lord Amado Carrillo.

text.p: Top Mexican drug lord Amado Carrillo Fuentes is dead, Mexican authorities confirmed on Thursday.

A DNA test confirmed that a man found dead in a Mexico City hospital last week was the 42-year-old Carrillo Fuentes, a man U.S. officials had described as the most powerful man in the booming Mexican drugs trade.
"We have arrived at...the positive identification of (the corpse as that of) Mr. Amado Carrillo Fuentes," Mariano Herran Salvatti, the head of Mexico's anti-drug agency, told reporters.
While fingerprints from the corpse matched those of the cocaine lord, the authorities were waiting for final proof of identity from a DNA test, Salvatti said at a news conference.

Carillo headed the so-called Juarez Cartel that smuggled tons of cocaine into the United States each year. Wanted on 26 separate charges by the U.S. Drugs Enforcement Agency, his death leaves a huge vacuum in the country's narco-trafficking industry.
Carrillo was nicknamed "Lord of the Skies" for his brazen tactic of jetting drugs into Mexico for shipment into the United States.
